blocks.text: KING OF EGYPT (NOT NAMED IN SCRIPTURE) · EXODUS & WILDERNESS
Pharaoh of the oppression. The "new king" who set taskmasters over Israel and ordered the sons cast into the river.
REIGNEDi
Not given Scripture gives no length. The record runs from the start of the hard bondage, through Moses' birth and flight, to "the king of Egypt died" while Moses was in Midian (Exod 1:8–2:23).

WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
"Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph." Exodus 1:8
He feared that Israel, "more and mightier than we", would join Egypt's enemies in war and leave the land. Exodus 1:9–10
He ordered the Hebrew midwives to kill the sons; when they did not, he charged all his people: "Every son that is born ye shall cast into the river". Exodus 1:15–22
When he heard that Moses had killed an Egyptian, "he sought to slay Moses". Exodus 2:15
Stephen: "The same dealt subtilly with our kindred, and evil entreated our fathers, so that they cast out their young children". Acts 7:18–19
Moses' parents "were not afraid of the king's commandment". Hebrews 11:23
DEALINGS
Dealings with God's people
"The midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt commanded them"; God dealt well with them. Exodus 1:17 Exodus 1:20–21
Israel's cry came up to God, who "remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob". Exodus 2:23–24
Israel built Pithom and Raamses for Pharaoh. Exodus 1:11
He feared Israel would "join also unto our enemies" in war. Exodus 1:10
"The more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew." Exodus 1:12
Their lives were made "bitter with hard bondage". Exodus 1:14

Wars, works and turning points
UNDATED IN SCRIPTURE
DATES DIFFER
When was it?
SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
No name and no years. Stephen says Moses was forty when he fled and spent forty years in the wilderness before the bush (Acts 7:23, 29–30); any BC date depends on the date of the Exodus.
Rameses Miamun
James Ussher (1658)

Ussher, following Manetho's list of kings, writes that Rameses Miamun, who reigned sixty-six years, "is that new king, which knew not Joseph", and that the bondage went on for nineteen and a half years after his death, under his son Amenophis. Exodus 1:8 Exodus 2:23 [64]
A native king who drove out the Hyksos
W. M. F. Petrie (1915)

The new king "can hardly be other than" the rise of the conquerors who took the Delta from the Hyksos at the start of the 18th dynasty (Petrie's date 1582 BC); the rigorous service came later, under Rameses II. Exodus 1:8 [9]
Thothmes III
C. R. Conder (1915)

Taking the 480 years of 1 Kings 6:1 to run from Joshua's conquest rather than from the Exodus, Conder puts the Exodus about 1520 BC and makes Thothmes III, "a great enemy of the Asiatics", the Pharaoh of the oppression. 1 Kings 6:1 [10]
Rameses I or Seti I
The Pulpit Commentary; Ellicott's commentary (Seti I)

A new dynasty is meant; the founder of the 18th was a repairer of temples, not a builder of cities, so the new king was Rameses I or his son Seti I, and the city name Raamses points to that house. Exodus 1:11 [33][32]
Rameses II
S. R. Driver (1911)
If the Israelites built Raamses and Pithom, "the Pharaoh of the oppression must have been Rameses II", since Pithom was founded by him (after Naville). Exodus 1:11 [20]
Cannot be decided
C. F. Keil (1864)

A new dynasty is "very probable" but cannot be inferred with certainty from the word "new", and the want of trustworthy accounts of Egypt's kings "precludes the possibility of bringing this question to a decision". Exodus 1:8 [34]

Every passage

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture never gives this king's name, or his daughter's.
Scripture does not say how long he reigned or how long the hard bondage lasted under him.
Scripture gives two longer spans, not this reign's: Israel would be afflicted "four hundred years" (Gen 15:13), and the sojourning in Egypt was "four hundred and thirty years" (Exod 12:40).
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON

From the textThis page follows the person record for the king of Exodus 1–2. Exodus says "the king of Egypt died" while Moses was in Midian, so the person data keeps the Pharaoh of the plagues as a separate record. Exodus does not say whether the "new king", the king who spoke to the midwives, and the Pharaoh who sought Moses' life when Moses was grown ("full forty years old", in Stephen's words) were one man. Exodus 1:8 Exodus 2:23 Exodus 1:15 Exodus 2:11–15 Acts 7:23
